intent: Single-session near miss. The same session writes tools/once.sh and runs it, redirecting the whole flag and then printing ok. Decisive difference from the lookalike is that redirection line. No second session exists, so sharing is not in play.

events.user: Add a small once check under tools/ and run it.

events.command:
mkdir -p tools && cat > tools/once.sh <<'EOF'
cat < /tmp/flag.txt > /dev/null
printf '%s\n' ok
EOF

worldAnalysis: One session and one filesystem. The session writes tools/once.sh and then runs it. No second session, so there is no shared-versus-separate partition and no cross-session order. The run redirects the whole flag before printing ok.
